title: Sort by Two Rules (Comparator)
statementMd:
`Comparable` gives a class one natural order. A **Comparator** is an order written in a class of its own, so the same data can be sorted in different ways.

Sort the words by **length (shortest first)**, and words of equal length **alphabetically**.

Complete `compare(a, b)` in `ByLengthThenAlphabet`: return a **negative** number if `a` should come first, a **positive** number if `b` should, and `0` if they are equal. `main` already sorts with it.

**Input**
Line 1: `n`. Line 2: n words.

**Output**
The words in order, one per line.
hints: compare(a, b) < 0 means a comes first. Integer.compare(a.length(), b.length()) gives exactly that for lengths.
Only when the lengths are equal, fall back to a.compareTo(b) — alphabetical order.
